name: GrowBikeNet
shortDescription: Grow bicycle networks from scratch or extend an existing network using greedy network growth strategies.
longDescription: GrowBikeNet simulates the incremental construction of bicycle networks from an existing network or from scratch to cover most of the city. Aiming to connect seed points like rail stations or schools, or just along a grid, it greedily adds streets following a triangulation or quadrangulation pattern. The suggested streets are then ordered based on a network centrality measure, for example to prioritize high-throughput corridors, and form the basis of a prioritized bicycle network. GrowBikeNet was validated across 62 cities worldwide and demonstrated that centrality-driven growth consistently outperforms random expansion.

usage.title: Install & Run it yourself
usage.code:
conda install growbikenet
python
import growbikenet as gbn
gbn.growbikenet('Lyon')

paper.title: Growing urban bicycle networks
paper.authors: M. Szell, S. Mimar, T. Perlman, G. Ghoshal, R. Sinatra

name: FixBikeNet
shortDescription: Detect and prioritize missing links in existing bicycle networks.
longDescription: FixBikeNet systematically finds gaps in already well-connected, existing bicycle infrastructure. It identifies where the bicycle network is missing links and prioritizes the most impactful ones. The result is an actionable list of surgical infrastructure investments that would most effectively improve network connectivity for the largest number of cycled kilometers. Originally demonstrated on Copenhagen's bicycle network.

usage.title: Install & Run it yourself
usage.code:
conda install fixbikenet
python
import fixbikenet as fbn
fbn.fixbikenet('Frederiksberg Municipality')

paper.title: Automated Detection of Missing Links in Bicycle Networks
paper.authors: A. Vybornova, T. Cunha, A. Gühnemann, M. Szell

name: LinkBikeNet
shortDescription: Connect fragmented, existing bicycle network pieces.
longDescription: LinkBikeNet uses data-driven strategies to determine the optimal order and placement of new bicycle links for maximum network connectedness. Rather than triangulating and building for an area like GrowBikeNet, it focuses only on connecting existing infrastructure — bridging isolated segments. The tool evaluates strategies like connecting the largest component to the nearest fragment, and compares them against real-world expansion patterns.

usage.title: Install & Run it yourself
usage.code:
conda install linkbikenet
python
import linkbikenet as lbn
lbn.linkbikenet('Budapest')

paper.title: Data-driven strategies for optimal bicycle network growth
paper.authors: L.G. Natera Orozco, F. Battiston, G. Iñiguez, M. Szell

name: SortBikeNet
shortDescription: Determine the best sequence for implementing a bicycle network plan.
longDescription: SortBikeNet tackles the sequencing problem: given a plan to build a bicycle network, in what order should segments be constructed to arrive at a functional network as soon as possible? The tool evaluates different construction orderings and has shown that optimal sequencing can yield at least a 3× better return on investment compared to how cities actually build their networks. It helps planners create phased implementation plans that deliver connectivity gains from the very first kilometer built.

name: superblockify
shortDescription: Partition urban street networks into potential superblock configurations.
longDescription: superblockify is a Python package that generates superblock-based partitions of urban street networks — car-free or traffic-calmed neighborhoods that prioritize pedestrians and cyclists. It visualizes alternative partitioning schemes and provides statistical analysis of each scenario, enabling planners to compare different superblock configurations for their city.

usage.title: Install & Run it yourself
usage.code:
conda install superblockify
python
import superblockify as sb
sb.ResidentialPartitioner(city_name='Scheveningen',search_str='Scheveningen, NL).run()

paper.title: superblockify: A Python Package for Automated Generation, Visualization, and Analysis of Potential Superblocks in Cities
paper.authors: C.M. Büth, A. Vybornova, M. Szell

name: BikeNetLib
shortDescription: The shared Python toolkit with general bicycle network utilities that powers the rest of the BikeNetKit family.
longDescription: BikeNetLib is the core utility package underpinning the BikeNetKit family of tools — shared input/output, network-analysis utilities, and visualization helpers built on OSMnx and GeoPandas, so GrowBikeNet, FixBikeNet, LinkBikeNet and the others don't each reimplement the same bicycle-network plumbing. It also provides general tools useful for anybody working with bicycle networks. BikeNetLib is developer/researcher-facing infrastructure rather than a standalone analysis: there is no visualization or dataset of its own, only a growing, documented API for anyone building on top of the family's tools. It is currently in early development.

name: MoveBikeNet
shortDescription: Trace how cyclists actually move, to reveal the routes they want rather than the ones they are given.
longDescription: MoveBikeNet uses computer vision and computational desire line analysis to understand actual cycling movement patterns. By analyzing observed trajectories from a video, it reveals where cyclists want to ride versus where infrastructure currently exists. The approach was originally demonstrated at the Dybbølsbro intersection in Copenhagen, one of Europe's busiest cycling junctions, showing how desire lines can inform intersection redesign and network planning.

paper.title: Computational Desire Line Analysis of Cyclists on the Dybbølsbro Intersection in Copenhagen
paper.authors: S.M. Breum, B. Kostic, M. Szell

name: BikeDNA
shortDescription: Assess the quality of bicycle infrastructure data by comparing OSM against reference datasets.
longDescription: BikeDNA is a tool for bicycle infrastructure data and network assessment. It compares OpenStreetMap bicycle data against official reference datasets at both global and local (grid cell) levels, measuring completeness, accuracy, and structural quality. The analysis produces interactive maps and reports. A "BIG" variant handles large-scale datasets. BikeDNA helps planners understand how reliable their data is before making infrastructure decisions.

paper.title: BikeDNA: A Tool for Bicycle Infrastructure Data & Network Assessment
paper.authors: A.R. Vierø, A. Vybornova, M. Szell

name: StretchBikeNet
shortDescription: Find the corridors worth stretching and upgrading, using optimal transport across a multilayer city network.
longDescription: StretchBikeNet addresses the challenge of designing cohesive urban bicycle infrastructure by modeling the city as a multilayer transport network. Using optimal transport routing, it identifies which corridors should be widened or upgraded to maximize cycling utility while accounting for interactions with other transport modes. The approach balances the trade-off between bicycle and car infrastructure, producing investment plans that improve the overall coherence of the cycling network.

paper.title: Cohesive urban bicycle infrastructure design through optimal transport routing in multilayer networks
paper.authors: A. Lonardi, M. Szell, C. De Bacco
paper.venue: Journal of the Royal Society Interface 22(223), 20240532

name: BikeNodePlanner
shortDescription: Evaluate a planned bicycle node network against the terrain, services and destinations around it.
longDescription: BikeNodePlanner is a decision-support tool for planning bicycle node networks — the numbered-signpost wayfinding systems that guide recreational cyclists along existing infrastructure. It runs in QGIS and Python and works for any study area. Planners feed it a draft network plan plus curated local geodata — land use, amenities, points of interest, elevation — and it returns a network analysis and a customisable evaluation against best-practice design criteria, both explorable interactively in QGIS. The result highlights the stretches that are too steep, too remote from services, or too poorly connected, so the plan can be adjusted before anything is signposted. It was built for users with minimal GIS experience, in a collaboration between Dansk Kyst- og Naturturisme and the IT University of Copenhagen to develop a country-wide bicycle node network for Denmark.

paper.title: BikeNodePlanner: A data-driven decision support tool for bicycle node network planning
paper.authors: A. Vybornova, A.R. Vierø, K.K. Hansen, M. Szell

name: LoopBikeNet
shortDescription: Take a census of the loops a node network offers, to see which round trips it actually makes possible.
longDescription: LoopBikeNet assesses the quality of a bicycle node network through loop census analysis. Rather than measuring the network segment by segment, it enumerates the closed round trips the network offers and characterises each by length, gradient, and the features along the way — the quantity that actually matters to a recreational cyclist choosing a day out. Applied to Denmark's 28,215 km country-wide node network, it revealed high heterogeneity and local clusters in node density, loop lengths, gradients and feature-rich areas: experienced cyclists have an abundance of options, while families with small children are sharply constrained by loop length and hilliness — a gap that e-bikes could close. The analysis runs on networks prepared with BikeNodePlanner.

paper.title: Quality assessment of a country-wide bicycle node network with loop census analysis
paper.authors: M. Szell, A. Vybornova, A.R. Vierø

name: HoodBikeNet
shortDescription: Grow the network neighbourhood by neighbourhood, linking low-traffic areas into one safe cycling web.
longDescription: HoodBikeNet extends bicycle network growth strategies to incorporate Low Traffic Neighbourhoods (LTNs). It combines modal filtering — restricting through-traffic in residential areas — with strategic bicycle network expansion, prioritizing connections between LTNs and existing cycling infrastructure. The tool helps planners maximize safe cycling coverage with minimal investment by leveraging the traffic-calmed environment that LTNs already provide.
